title: Real-time traffic sampler + evaluation feedback loop with automated rollback orchestrator
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Ship a deterministically-sampled traffic path that feeds a lightweight online evaluation pipeline (A/B and canary) and a decision engine that can trigger automated rollbacks when quality regressions exceed configured thresholds. This is intended to protect customer-facing routes from model/config regressions introduced by new deployments or runtime config changes (temperature, quantization profile, KV cache behavior).

Scope:
- Implement a traffic-sampler component (path in the proxy/router) that mirrors a configurable percentage of live requests to a background evaluation pipeline without increasing user-observed latency.
- Run lightweight, production-alike evals on mirrored traffic (decoding truncated for cost) and compute per-request quality signals (BLEU/ROUGE-like where applicable, embedding-similarity, rerank AUC, hallucination heuristics).
- Maintain rolling-window statistics and perform A/B hypothesis testing with configurable sensitivity (frequentist t-test + optional bayesian credible intervals).
- Decision engine that evaluates alerts, supports staged actions: notify -> pause rollout -> automatic rollback -> quarantine model variant.
- Orchestrator hooks into rollout controller to enact rollbacks and emits audit logs for Private deployments.

Non-goals: full fidelity evaluation of long-form outputs (costly), replacing offline evals, re-training models.
acceptance_criteria: Traffic sampler can mirror 0.1% to 5% of production requests with <1% extra CPU on the proxy tier
Evaluation pipeline computes the configured signal for mirrored requests within 30s median processing latency
Decision engine enforces rollback when configured delta exceeds threshold for 5 consecutive windows
Rollbacks performed via rollout API and logged to audit trail; rollback success/failure surfaced in console
Can run in Hosted and Dedicated modes; VPC/private audit logs produced for Private deployments
technical_approach: Sampler: deterministic hash-based sampling at the edge using request id + deployment id to ensure repeatability across retries
Mirror path: async copy over a thrift/gRPC internal topic (Kafka or internal queue) so requests do not block user response path
Lightweight evals: sample truncated outputs (first N tokens + embeddings) and run fast heuristics + embedding similarity to pinned references
Metrics & stats: time-windowed aggregations written to Prometheus and BigQuery for offline debugging; use an intermediate Redis ring to keep rolling-window state
Decision engine: policy DSL (JSON) with conditions, severity, and actions. Default policy uses two-sided t-test on mean quality with alpha=0.01 and min sample size 200
Orchestrator: integrates with existing rollout controller (ENG-7619) via gRPC and supports canary abort, pause, and rollback actions. All actions require idempotency and exponential backoff
tradeoffs_and_risks: Cost vs coverage: higher mirror % gives better signal but increases egress/cost. Default 1% is conservative.
Signal fidelity: using truncated outputs and embeddings is cheaper but may miss regressions in long-form generation
Statistical guarantees: small canary sizes risk false positives/negatives; policy includes min sample and holdout checks
Privacy: mirrored requests must be scrubbed of PII; for Private deployments we respect KMS policies and do not persist raw texts longer than 24h
implementation_plan: Week 1: Prototype sampler + async mirror pipeline, integration test that mirrored traffic arrives at eval worker
Week 2: Implement lightweight eval heuristics + rolling-window aggregation, basic dashboard in Grafana
Week 3: Decision engine DSL + connectors to rollout controller, integration tests for rollback path
Week 4: Hardening, privacy filters, add audit logs for Private deployments, run canary internally on non-critical routes
Post-ship: iterate thresholds based on observed false positive rate and extend eval metrics set
monitoring_and_alerting: Grafana dashboard: per-deployment quality delta, sample size, CI width, rollback actions history (link placeholder: https://grafana.internal/redwood/eval-rollout)
Pager alert: triggered if decision engine auto-rollbacks > 3 in 24h for a single model
SLOs: evaluation pipeline availability 99.9%, decision latency <60s
Audit logs: every automated action emits an immutable audit entry (link to logging console: https://logs.internal/redwood/query?query=eval_rollback)
Daily summary report to PMs with false positive/negative estimates and impacted customer routes
test_plan: Unit tests for sampler hashing and determinism
Load tests that mirror 5% of synthetic traffic to ensure system scales with less than 5% CPU overhead on proxy
Canary exercise: deploy a controlled regression to a canary and assert the decision engine rolls back within configured window
Chaos test: simulate queue loss and verify mirrored traffic is backfilled and decision engine tolerates temporary gaps
